targetReport.description: The organic law establishing the formula for splitting non-retroceded public revenues between the Union government and the three Autonomous Islands (Ngazidja/Grande Comore, Anjouan, Mohéli). targetReport.title: Property Assessment Notice and Assessment Roll (Current Value Assessment)
targetReport.description: Ontario's single province-wide property assessment, prepared by a not-for-profit corporation funded by all Ontario municipalities rather than by a government department. This is the structural difference from Alberta, where each municipality prepares its own roll and the province must then run an explicit equalization step to make them comparable. Ontario needs no equalization because there is one assessor. The standard is Current Value, defined in the Assessment Act s. 1(1) as 'the amount of money the fee simple, if unencumbered, would realize if sold at arm's length by a willing seller to a willing buyer'. MPAC states it uses 'one of three approaches to value properties: direct comparison approach, income approach, cost approach', with the direct comparison approach 'the most commonly used' and the choice depending on 'property type, and the number of recent comparable sales of similar properties in the area'. The returned roll and its household counts are what the Ontario Municipal Partnership Fund allocates against.
targetReport.cadence_note: The roll returns annually; the values in it have not been re-based since 2016, and the gap between those two facts is the point. The Assessment Act s. 19.2(1) sets a four-year cycle by schedule, and para 4 assigns 1 January 2016 to 'the four taxation years from 2017 to 2020'. MPAC states the schedule has been suspended: 'On August 16, 2023, the Ontario government filed a regulation to amend the Assessment Act, extending the postponement of a province-wide reassessment through the end of the 2021-2024 assessment cycle. Property assessments for the 2026 property tax year will continue to be based on fully phased-in January 1, 2016 current values.' So `releases_per_year` 1 counts the returned roll, which does move for new construction, demolition and change of use; `changes_per_year` 0.25 is the statutory reassessment cycle, which is the rate at which the valuation basis is supposed to move and has not moved in ten years. Both numbers are true and neither alone describes this node.

targetReport.title: EAC Regulations for Compiling Harmonised Consumer Price Indices (HCPI)
targetReport.description: A binding East African Community instrument (March 2022) requiring Partner States to compile and submit a Harmonised CPI to the EAC Secretariat, for regional comparability and East African Monetary Union convergence-criteria monitoring -- described as binding in its entirety and directly applicable, and classification 'shall be based on the most recent official United Nations Classification of Individual Consumption According to Purpose (COICOP)'. Filed `supranational` rather than `international` on the same reasoning the corpus already applies to the EU's ESA 2010: a regional body legislating a binding, directly-applicable obligation, not a standard adopted by choice. Distinct from Kenya's own domestic CPI, which aligns with these regulations' spirit (per KNBS's own rebasing report) without the regulations themselves directly governing the domestic release -- the binding obligation is to also produce the separate HCPI submission.

release_schedule.note: This is a one-off legal/regulatory instrument (EAC Regulations for Compiling Harmonised Consumer Price Indices, published March 2022), not a recurring statistical publication. The document itself was 'gazetted' with a target entry-into-force date of 31 Dec 2024 (Article 106), a one-time milestone, not a recurring cycle. Internally it does specify review cycles for the underlying CPI methodology (weights reviewed at max 5-year intervals per Art. 704.1, mini-surveys every 2-3 years per Art. 704.2, EAC-level weights every 3-5 years per Art. 706.5, annual compliance reports per Art. 113.3), but none of these are a stated periodicity for reissuing or amending the Regulations document itself. There is no found evidence of a fixed amendment/republication cadence for the Regulations text, so releases_per_year probably should not be treated as a fixed number for this report at all -- it is better modeled as irregular (amended only when the EAC Council/Secretariat decides to revise it) rather than assigned any specific interval.

targetReport.title: Constitution of the Republic of South Africa, 1996 — Chapter 13 (Finance)
targetReport.description: The constitutional basis for how revenue is split among South Africa's three spheres of government. VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session. s.213: money raised nationally goes into the National Revenue Fund, and 'a province's equitable share of revenue raised nationally' is 'a direct charge against the National Revenue Fund'. s.214(1)(a): 'An Act of Parliament must provide for... the equitable division of revenue raised nationally among the national, provincial and local spheres of government'; s.214(2) lists the factors that Act must weigh, including provinces' and municipalities' ability to 'provide basic services' and 'fiscal capacity and efficiency'. s.226 gives each province its own Revenue Fund; s.227(1)(a) entitles local government and provinces to 'an equitable share of revenue raised nationally... to provide basic services'. ss.228-229 give provinces and municipalities limited own-revenue powers (no income tax, VAT or customs duty for either).
